leftEvidence.title: David appears inside a rapid witness catalogue

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The chapter names Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and prophets before describing victories, suffering, death, and an unreceived promise shared with later readers.
points.right: The holy and true speaker holds David’s key, opens and shuts, sets an open door, knows little power and faithful confession, promises vindication and preservation, and names a future pillar.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David is one name within a deliberately compressed and internally varied memory inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Isaiah’s key language is reused in a promise-bearing address inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Hebrews 11:32–40 and Revelation 3:7–13 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: The one with David’s key addresses Philadelphia

payload.tension: Hebrews 11:32–40 foregrounds David is one name within a deliberately compressed and internally varied memory; Revelation 3:7–13 foregrounds Isaiah’s key language is reused in a promise-bearing address. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
